nodes.label: Stale Cache / Service Worker Recovery Pattern
nodes.rationale: Avoids automatic cache-cleanup reloads because some mobile browsers do not persist the migration marker reliably, which can trap visitors in a reload loop before React mounts. Instead, a 20s timeout plus a MutationObserver/error listener detects a failed boot (React never mounted, stale chunks) and shows a manual 'Bersihkan & muat ulang' button that unregisters service workers and clears Cache Storage before reloading, keeping login state intact.
nodes.norm_label: stale cache / service worker recovery pattern

nodes.label: TODO[backend-pending] Dummy-Data Convention
nodes.rationale: For new admin pages (Revenue, Apps, PWA Vitals, Android ANR, Audit) whose backend endpoints don't exist yet, frontend hooks (e.g. useAdminRevenue()) mirror the real API signature but return constant dummy data copied from the artboard. Each hook is tagged with a `// TODO[backend-pending]` comment naming the expected endpoint and response shape, and pages show a dev-only amber warning banner. This lets the UI ship pixel-perfect immediately while keeping dummy implementations trackable and preventing them from silently masquerading as real data, with all pending endpoints consolidated into IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md.

nodes.label: ADR-001: PII Encryption Strategy (AES-256 + SHA-256 Hash Columns)
nodes.rationale: Pure encryption blocks indexed lookup (email/phone login, uniqueness checks); bcrypt is too slow for lookups and can't be used in SQL WHERE clauses. Solution: dual-column strategy per PII field — AES-256-GCM `_enc` column for storage/decryption, deterministic SHA-256 `_hash` column for indexed equality lookup. Trade-off accepted: SHA-256 hashes of common emails are theoretically rainbow-table attackable, but hashes are only used for equality lookup and never exposed in API responses. Changing ENCRYPTION_KEY requires a full re-encryption migration (high-stakes event). Redis is forbidden from ever caching `*email*`, `*phone*`, `*password*` keys.
nodes.norm_label: adr-001: pii encryption strategy (aes-256 + sha-256 hash columns)

nodes.label: ADR-002: JWT Session Management with Redis Revocation
nodes.rationale: Stateless JWTs can't support instant single-logout, logout-all-devices, or admin-initiated session kill. Two-layer Redis-backed revocation chosen over MySQL blocklist or short-expiry+refresh tokens: (1) per-token JTI revocation (`jti:{jti} -> revoked`, TTL = remaining token life) for single logout; (2) `session_version:user:{id}` counter for O(1) bulk logout-all/password-change/admin-suspend invalidation. Trade-off: adds ~1ms latency per request (two Redis reads); if Redis is down and REDIS_FEATURE_SESSIONS=false, revocation is bypassed as an accepted degradation. Separate JWT secrets (JWT_SECRET vs ADMIN_JWT_SECRET) make user and admin tokens mutually unusable.
nodes.norm_label: adr-002: jwt session management with redis revocation

nodes.label: ADR-003: Asynq on Redis for Background Job Queue
nodes.rationale: Synchronous email sending in HTTP handlers would couple response latency to Resend API availability and provide no retry mechanism. Asynq on the already-required Redis instance was chosen over a DB-polling worker or a dedicated MQ (RabbitMQ/SQS) because it needs no new infrastructure and provides built-in retry/DLQ. Trade-off: Asynq's `asynq:*` keys share Redis with session/rate-limit data under an `allkeys-lru` eviction policy, risking eviction of queued jobs under memory pressure if queue volume grows; a separate worker binary (`apps/backend/cmd/worker/`) must be deployed and monitored independently.
nodes.norm_label: adr-003: asynq on redis for background job queue

nodes.label: ADR-005: Separate Admin Backend Service
nodes.rationale: Admin routes inside the user backend, or a user backend accepting an elevated role claim, both risk a JWT-role-check bug escalating a user token to admin. Chose a fully separate `apps/admin-backend` service with a distinct JWT secret (ADMIN_JWT_SECRET), distinct database (sawit_hub_admin_db), distinct Vercel domain (adminpanel.sawithub.com, robots-blocked), and distinct CORS origin — making cross-service token reuse structurally impossible rather than policy-enforced. Trade-off: two services to deploy/maintain; shared ENCRYPTION_KEY still required so admin can decrypt user PII for support; some middleware/logger/OTel code is intentionally duplicated rather than shared, to keep each service independently deployable.

nodes.label: ADR-006: MySQL Generated Columns for Derived Financial Values
nodes.rationale: Computing derived financial fields (berat_ton, berat_rata_janjang, total_pendapatan, hasil_bersih, pendapatan_bersih) in the application layer or as manually-updated columns risks divergence from source columns across multiple write paths. Chose MySQL `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (...) STORED` columns so the DB engine guarantees consistency by construction, can be indexed, and appears in SELECT *, with zero application logic. Trade-off: changing a formula requires a migration; STORED columns use disk space like regular columns; developers unfamiliar with generated columns may try to INSERT/UPDATE them and hit a confusing MySQL error (documented in handler comments); division-by-zero (jumlah_janjang=0) correctly resolves to NULL.
nodes.norm_label: adr-006: mysql generated columns for derived financial values

nodes.label: ADR-007: Trunk-Based Development with Path-Filtered CI
nodes.rationale: GitFlow's long-lived branches cause merge conflicts and overhead for a small team across four deployable services in one monorepo. Chose trunk-based development (short-lived 1-3 day branches merging directly to main) combined with GitHub Actions `paths:` filters so each service's CI only runs when its own files change, keeping main always deployable and CI time proportional to the diff. Trade-off: requires discipline to keep branches short; no feature-flag system yet exists for in-flight multi-PR work (tracked as backlog debt); emergency hotfixes follow the same branch->PR->main path, meaning all in-flight main work ships alongside a hotfix.
nodes.norm_label: adr-007: trunk-based development with path-filtered ci
